title: How a Debate Outline Works
text:
A debate outline helps speakers organize their arguments before a competition. It usually starts with an introduction that states the topic and the position. After that, the outline lists three main points, each supported by evidence. Students often write the outline on one page so it is easy to read during the debate.

The last part of the outline is the conclusion. In this section, the speaker repeats the main position and summarizes the best evidence. Many teachers say a good conclusion should be short, clear, and strong. Some students also prepare answers to possible questions from the other team.

questions.text: How many main points does the outline list?
What do many teachers say about a good conclusion?
options: It should be long and detailed
It should be short, clear, and strong
It should be read in a loud voice
It should not repeat any evidence

questions.text: Why do students write the outline on one page?
options: So they can read it easily during the debate
Because the teacher requires it for grades
So they can hide it from the other team
Because the debate lasts only one minute

questions.text: What is the main purpose of the conclusion?
options: To remind the audience of the main position
To ask the other team questions

vocabulary.definition: a short plan that shows the main points of something
reasons given to support an opinion or position
facts or information that show something is true
the final part of a speech or text that sums up the main points

paragraph_translations: Un esquema de debate ayuda a los oradores a organizar sus argumentos antes de una competición. Normalmente empieza con una introducción que presenta el tema y la postura. Después, el esquema enumera tres puntos principales, cada uno apoyado por pruebas. Los estudiantes suelen escribir el esquema en una sola página para leerlo fácilmente durante el debate.

La última parte del esquema es la conclusión. En esta sección, el orador repite la postura principal y resume las mejores pruebas. Muchos profesores dicen que una buena conclusión debe ser breve, clara y contundente. Algunos estudiantes también preparan respuestas a posibles preguntas del otro equipo.
